condition_specific: bladder, brain, breast, cervical, colon, esophageal, invasive skin, kidney, large intestinal, lung, malignant melanoma, mesothelioma, multiple myeloma, non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, oral cavity/pharynx, ovarian, prostate, rectal, stomach, testicular, thyroid cancer
notes: Covers full-time firefighters only (not volunteer). Must not have used tobacco products for at least 5 preceding years. Must not have been employed in a higher-risk position in the preceding 5 years. Benefits include employer-sponsored health plan coverage (with out-of-pocket reimbursement) and $25,000 one-time cash payout on initial diagnosis. Post-termination coverage available for 10 years if eligibility criteria met at termination and not subsequently employed as firefighter. This is an alternative to WC under chapter 440. Effective July 1, 2019. CONFIRMED (2026-08-07 research): Ch. 2026-99 (SB 984, signed by the Governor May 22, 2026, Ch. assigned May 26, 2026) amends § 112.1816(4)(c) to extend the cancer death-benefit obligation to a firefighter's former employer for 1 year after the firefighter's termination date, provided the firefighter otherwise met all program eligibility criteria at termination and was not subsequently re-employed as a firefighter. This closes a gap in which a firefighter who developed covered cancer, left employment, and died within a year of leaving service could previously fall outside any employer's death-benefit obligation. Confirmed via the bill's official Senate history page and enrolled-bill text analysis. Effective July 1, 2026.

notes: Employee must file written affidavit declaring no outside exposure. Pre-employment exam required (testing for hepatitis/TB; meningitis exempt from exam requirement). filing_deadline_notes: Claim must be properly noticed within 52 weeks after qualifying event
notes: PTSD is a compensable occupational disease. Must be diagnosed by a licensed psychiatrist who is an authorized treating physician. Must result from one of enumerated qualifying events (e.g., death of a minor, grievous bodily harm). No physical injury required. Not subject to apportionment for pre-existing PTSD. Effective October 1, 2018. Also covers volunteer firefighters.

condition_specific: Smallpox vaccination adverse effects (deemed a compensable injury arising out of employment)
notes: Any adverse result or complication from a smallpox vaccination given to a first responder is deemed a workplace injury by accident. This provision was originally enacted in 2007 (Ch. 2007-87), arising from federal/state smallpox pre-event vaccination programs, and predates the 2018 amendment that added PTSD coverage to a different part of the same statute (§ 112.1815) -- the two provisions have separate origin dates. It's narrow in practical scope, applying only during an active smallpox vaccination program, but it remains in effect, with no repeal or sunset found. It also covers volunteer firefighters.
